overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve minutes for its January 11 and 30, 2024 meetings, found the other minutes timely, and ordered immediate and future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee failed to timely approve minutes of meetings held January 11 and January 30, 2024.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee failed to timely approve the minutes of its meetings held on January 11 and 30.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee failed to timely approve minutes of meetings held December 5, 2023 and January 17 and February 1, 2024.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee timely approved all other minutes at issue in the complaint.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged minutes for several meetings were not posted to the Town's website.
allegations.key_passage: the complainant is aware that the Open Meeting Law does not require that minutes be posted to a website.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with G.L. c. 30A, § 22(c) and 940 CMR 29.11 (timely approval of open session minutes), with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent and may result in a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per violation.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance, and caution that a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law and may result in a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per violation.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
